beats.narration: Chapter 16, on tumour immunology, had 28 claims for me, and 12 needed revision. For Chapters 11 and 15, I decided to rule on every sentence myself, not just the flagged ones. That is 233 sentences in Chapter 11 and 518 in Chapter 15. In Chapter 11, 13 of the 90 checked claims needed revision. In Chapter 15, 28 of 238.

beats.new_visual_element: What a reader sees and the checker cannot
beats.narration: When I looked at why the check missed the repeats, the answer was in the workbook data. Chapter 16 prints a 170-word paragraph twice in a row, and Chapter 11 prints one caption under two photos. Duplicates had been removed before checking, so the second copy was never in front of the checker at all. Chapter 15 repeats eleven more sentences.

beats.new_visual_element: How often the cleared sentences were wrong
beats.narration: Ruling on every sentence also let me measure something I had wondered about: how often the sentences the system did not flag were wrong. In Chapter 11, 14.4 percent of flagged claims needed revision, and so did 5.6 percent of the unflagged ones. In Chapter 15, 11.8 percent against 1.8. The flags find most of the errors. The rest is not clean.

beats.new_visual_element: Flags that would have added errors
beats.narration: Some flags would have made the book worse if I had simply applied them. One wanted to change a chemical name to the wrong form of the compound; I checked it against PubChem. One called a real 43-patient trial made up, and would have deleted it; I found the trial. One called an author invented, when the name was only misspelled.

beats.new_visual_element: One cancer's finding filed under another
beats.narration: Chapter 15 kept attaching findings from one cancer to another, seven times. A radiation-resistance finding from ovarian cancer shows up four times under lung cancer. Liver cancer results sit in the colorectal section. The flags caught four of the seven. I found the other three by reading the sources.

resolver.label: ONE CANCER'S FINDING, FILED UNDER ANOTHER
resolver.detail: Seven times in Chapter 15. Four were flagged; three were not.

beats.narration: What these chapters taught me is to ask what a check never sees: repeated text, the wrong cancer, sentences it decided were safe. My own sentences went through the same test, and nine of them across Chapters 11 and 15 had to be rewritten. All three chapters' corrections are now merged into the textbook.
